parsed.explanation: Dependent territory: derive from the parent regime, which applies directly here. Worst documented exposure is custody placement by identity-document marker, which in practice puts trans women in all-male facilities where they face threats. The watchdog's 2021 findings of persistent serious violations, based on about 40 referrals since 2010, are recurring oversight findings with no documented remedy, so they corroborate an unremedied exposure. Mitigations are real but largely unevidenced on the island: anti-discrimination and transphobia-aggravation law (in force since 2016-17), simplified gender change, conversion-therapy ban, and marriage equality, though the dossier records no island enforcement record. Visitor-facing friction (services, lawyers, healthcare access) is thin or open. The 2020 attack figure is national and cannot be used. Border and facility rules are not documented as restrictive. Net: Elevated Risk, held up by the parent's protections and held down by custody exposure.
